This page documents [`data/synthetic-periodicals.csv`](../data/synthetic-periodicals.csv). It is the worked answer to the user story **E08-S1** in the [example backlog](../project-management/backlog.md#e08).

::: {.callout-important}
## Every record is synthetic

The 30 records describe periodicals that never existed. A script invented the titles, the publishers, the dates, and the reuse status. Do not cite these records as historical evidence.
:::

## Overview

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| File | `data/synthetic-periodicals.csv` |
| Format | CSV, UTF-8, comma-separated, one header row |
| Records | 30, one row per fictional periodical |
| Version | 1.0.0 (12 October 2026) |
| Origin | Generated by [`src/generate_synthetic_periodicals.py`](https://github.com/maehr/github-as-a-project-management-tool/blob/main/src/generate_synthetic_periodicals.py) with the fixed seed 2026 |
| Licence | [CC BY 4.0](../LICENSE-CCBY.md) |
| Personal data | None |
| Author | Moritz Mähr |

## Missing values

A missing value is an **empty cell**. The dataset uses no placeholder text such as `NA`, `unknown`, or `0` for a missing value.

| Column | Records with an empty cell | Meaning of the empty cell |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `last_year` | SYN-P004, SYN-P011, SYN-P017, SYN-P023, SYN-P029 | The last year of publication is not known. |
| `publisher` | SYN-P008, SYN-P019, SYN-P026 | The publisher is not known. |
| `frequency` | SYN-P013, SYN-P027 | The frequency of publication is not known. |

The value `unknown` in `scan_reuse_status` is not a missing value. It states that the fictional archive gave no reuse terms.

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description | Allowed values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `record_id` | string | Unique identifier of the record | `SYN-P` followed by three digits, for example `SYN-P001` |
| `title` | string | Title of the fictional periodical | Free text |
| `language` | string | Main language of the periodical | ISO 639-1 code: `de`, `fr`, `it` |
| `place_of_publication` | string | Town of publication | Free text |
| `first_year` | integer | First year of publication | 1830 to 1905 |
| `last_year` | integer | Last year of publication | Equal to or later than `first_year`; empty if not known |
| `frequency` | string | Frequency of publication | `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `irregular`; empty if not known |
| `subject` | string | Main subject | `politics`, `culture`, `religion`, `economy`, `science`, `entertainment` |
| `publisher` | string | Fictional publisher or printer | Free text; empty if not known |
| `scan_reuse_status` | string | Reuse terms that the fictional archive gives for its scans | `open`, `attribution-required`, `unknown`, `restricted` |
| `digitised` | string | Whether the fictional archive has digitised the periodical | `yes`, `no`, `partial` |
| `is_synthetic` | boolean | Marks the record as synthetic | `true` for every record |

## The restricted record

Record **SYN-P021** has `scan_reuse_status` = `restricted`. Exercise [X6](../course/exercises/x6.qmd) uses this record: the fictional archive restricts reuse of its scans. The restriction applies to the fictional scans, not to this CSV. The CSV stays under CC BY 4.0.

## Reuse

1. Download the CSV from the repository or from a release.
2. Cite the course as [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/maehr/github-as-a-project-management-tool/blob/main/CITATION.cff) describes.
3. Keep the column `is_synthetic` in every copy, so that nobody mistakes the records for real data.
